title: Direct and Indirect Culture Methods for Studying Biodegradable Implant Materials In Vitro
protocol: Euthanize the Sprague Dawley (SD) rat by CO2 inhalation.
Remove skin and muscle and connective tissues from the euthanized rat.
Dissect the femur out of the euthanized rat.
Place the femoral bones in a 15 mL conical tube containing cell culture medium.
Place the conical tubes on ice until the time of performing cell extraction.
Transfer bones to a Petri dish in the biological safety cabinet.
Cut the ends of the bone using a surgical blade.
Flush the bone marrow into a 50 mL conical tube by washing the bone marrow cavity with cell culture media using a syringe with a 25½ G needle.
Insert a syringe with an 18 G needle into the media containing bone marrow.
Slowly and gently take up and dispense the media to break apart large chunks of marrow until no visible cell/tissue agglomerates are present.
Filter the cell suspension using a 70 µm filter.
Centrifuge at 126 × g (1,000 rpm) for 5 min to obtain cell pellets.
Aspirate the supernatant media and replenish with 10 mL of fresh media.
Gently pipette up and down to resuspend cells using a 10 mL serological pipette.
Pipette the suspension directly onto the inside bottom of a T-75 flask.
Add media to bring the volume up to 25 mL.
Culture cells in an incubator under standard sterile cell culture conditions (37 °C, humidified atmosphere with 5% CO2 and 95% air).
Rinse away nonadherent cells by aspirating old medium after 3-7 days and replenishing with fresh medium.
Continue culturing and feeding cells with fresh medium until they are ready for cell passage, freezing, or use in an experiment.
Change the cell culture medium regularly every other day until the cells reach 90%-100% confluency.
Check the cells under an optical microscope when they are approximately 90% confluent.
Aspirate the medium from the cell flask.
Dispense 10 mL of phosphate-buffered saline (PBS) into the flask using a serological pipette.
Gently rock the flask to rinse the cells with PBS; aspirate all the PBS.
Dispense 3 mL of trypsin-EDTA into the cell flask directly onto the surface of the cells.
Gently rock the flask to ensure the entire surface with the cells is covered by the trypsin-EDTA.
Place the cell flask with trypsin-EDTA into the incubator for 5 min.
Incubate the cells for 5 minutes in the incubator.
Check the cells under an optical microscope to confirm detachment.
Tap the side of the cell flask gently if some cells have not detached, then check again.
Add 9 mL of fresh medium to the cell flask to dilute trypsin-EDTA.
Pipette out the cells in media and trypsin-EDTA and dispense them into a 15 mL conical tube.
Centrifuge the cells at 126 × g (1,000 rpm) for 5 min.
Aspirate the medium with trypsin-EDTA from the centrifuge tube without disturbing the cell pellet.
Add 5-10 mL of fresh media to the centrifuge tube and gently resuspend the cells using a 10 mL serological pipette.
Pipette the cells suspended in medium out of the centrifuge tube and split into 2-3 fresh culture flasks.
Add enough medium to bring the total volume to 25 mL for each flask.
Check the cells under an optical microscope before placing them back into the incubator.
Confirm that the cells are 90% confluent under an optical microscope.
Repeat steps of cell detachment, trypsin-EDTA addition, and centrifugation as described.
Add 900 µL of fresh medium to the centrifuge tube with a micropipette.
Gently resuspend cells in medium using the same micropipette.
Transfer the 900 µL cell suspension into a cryovial.
Add 100 µL of dimethylsulfoxide (DMSO) to the cryovial.
Place the cryovial in a cylindrical foam container designed for temperature regulation.
Place the foam container in the -80 °C freezer.
Thaw the frozen cells in a water bath.
Take a sterile 15 mL conical tube filled with 5 mL of fresh medium and place the thawed cells into it.
Centrifuge the contents at 126 × g (1,000 rpm) for 5 min.
Aspirate the medium containing DMSO from the conical tube.
Add 5-10 mL of fresh medium to the conical tube with the pellet.
Slowly and gently pipette up and down to resuspend the cells in the new medium.
Pipette the cells suspended in medium out of the 15 mL conical tube.
Dispense the cell suspension into a new T-75 flask using a sweeping motion.
Add enough fresh medium to bring the total volume to 25 mL for each T-75 flask.
Check the cells under an optical microscope.
Place the cell flask back into the incubator.
Disinfect biodegradable metals using ultraviolet radiation for in vitro studies.
Sterilize Mg alloy samples under dry heat in an oven or autoclave at the temperature range of 100-200 °C.
Disinfect biodegradable polymers using UV radiation or 70% ethanol before use in cell studies.
Sterilize polymers with gamma-ray treatment, such as Cobalt-60 radiation, if necessary.
Autoclave polymer materials that can withstand high temperature and moisture.
Use EtO gas to sterilize polymeric materials sensitive to heat or radiation.
Follow steps 1.2.2.1-1.2.2.10 to obtain the cell suspension.
Determine the cell concentration in the cell suspension using a hemocytometer from a 90% confluent flask.
Dilute the cell suspension with fresh medium to the prescribed cell concentration needed for the study.
Rinse the culture plates with 2 mL of PBS and 2 mL of DMEM sequentially under sterile conditions.
Add 3 mL of the diluted cell suspension into each well onto the samples of interest.
Culture the cells in an incubator under standard cell culture conditions for 24 h.
Rinse the cells in the well plate with PBS using a pipette to remove floating dead cells.
Place disinfected or sterilized samples directly on the adhered cells.
Add 3 mL of fresh medium into each well.
Culture the cells under standard cell culture conditions for another 24 h.
Collect the postculture medium from each well into a corresponding 15 mL conical tube for further analysis.
Rinse the cells adherent on both samples and well plates 3 times using PBS.
Add 1 ml of 4% paraformaldehyde (PFA, 10% neutral buffered formalin) into each well plate.
Put the lid back on the well plate and allow the PFA to react for 20 min.
Aspirate the PFA and dispense it into a waste bottle.
Rinse the well plate 3 times using PBS to remove the PFA, and transfer the waste to the waste bottle.
Prepare the working stocks of the staining agents following the manufacturers' instructions.
Add 200-400 μl of diluted Alexa Fluor 488 Phalloidin staining agent to each well to cover the cells on the well plate and the sample.
Wrap the well plate in aluminum foil to prevent light exposure, and allow the Alexa Fluor 488 Phalloidin to react for 20 min at room temperature.
Collect Alexa Fluor 488 Phalloidin staining agent and dispense it into the corresponding waste bottle.
Rinse the well plate 3 times using PBS to remove excess Alexa Fluor 488 Phalloidin, and dispense used PBS into the corresponding waste bottle.
Add 200-400 µL of diluted DAPI to each well to cover cells in the well and on the sample.
Wrap the well plate in aluminum foil and allow DAPI to react for 5 min at room temperature.
Collect the DAPI and dispense it into the corresponding waste bottle.
Rinse the well plate 3 times using PBS to remove DAPI, and dispense used PBS into the corresponding waste bottle.
Image cells using a fluorescence microscope after staining.
Take phase-contrast images of cells whenever possible in addition to fluorescence images.
Image cells on biodegradable samples as soon as possible or immediately after staining.
Store cells in well plates in buffer solution at 2-8 °C after fixation.
Image and evaluate two types of cells: (1) the cells on the samples and (2) the cells adherent on the well plate surrounding the samples.
Use an image guide when taking fluorescence images of cells.
Image and analyze the cells located in the area within the inner ring (3.5 mm away from the center) separately.
Image and analyze the cells located in the area within the outer ring (7 mm away from the center) separately.
Take at least five images from each area of interest where the cells are either in direct contact or indirect contact with the samples at a predefined distance.
Quantify cell morphology by measuring the cell spreading area using software such as ImageJ for image analysis.
Measure the aspect ratio of cells using software such as ImageJ for image analysis.
Count the number of cells in each image area.
Calculate the cell adhesion density under direct and indirect contact conditions as the number of cells per unit area.
Measure the pH of postculture medium.
Measure the pH value of the postculture medium immediately after collection using a precalibrated pH meter.
Analyze the medium compositions for the degradation behavior of biodegradable samples.
For some samples that cause a color change, measure the optical density (O.D.) value of the postculture medium using a spectrophotometer or microplate reader.

Alternatively, use ultraviolet-visible spectroscopy (UV-VIS) and Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy-attenuated total reflectance (FTIR-ATR) to analyze degradation products in the postculture medium.
Measure the concentrations of ions of interest in the postculture medium using an ICP-OES after collecting and diluting the medium for optimal measurements.
Take photographs of the samples after cell culture to show changes in dimension, color, and morphology.
Dry or dehydrate the postculture samples.
Measure the mass, dimension, and volume of the dried samples.
Use a scanning electron microscope (SEM) to characterize the microstructure and morphology of the samples.
Use energy dispersive X-Ray spectroscopy (EDX) to characterize the composition of the degradation products on the samples.
Use X-ray diffraction (XRD) to determine the phase of the degradation products on the samples.
Use FTIR-ATR to detect chemical bonding on the sample surfaces.
